ic_name: USB4 (USB Implementers Forum, Intel Thunderbolt 3 base)

device_visible_states.name: Disconnected
device_visible_states.description: No partner detected on the USB-C link; SBU + CC monitoring only.

device_visible_states.name: Training
device_visible_states.description: LT-LFPS link training + lane bonding in progress.

device_visible_states.name: Connected
device_visible_states.description: High-speed link up; router visible to the Connection Manager.

device_visible_states.name: Enumerated
device_visible_states.description: Connection Manager has read the router's config space and placed it in the spanning tree.

device_visible_states.name: Configured
device_visible_states.description: Paths/tunnels set up; adapters enabled; tunneled traffic flowing.

device_visible_states.name: Sleep/Low-power
device_visible_states.description: Link in a low-power state (e.g. USB4 sleep); resumes via SBU/LFPS.

fsm_hints.host_role: The host router hosts the Connection Manager, which discovers routers, allocates hop IDs, and programs paths/tunnels.
fsm_hints.router_role: Each router forwards tunneled + control packets per its installed path configuration; lane adapters bring up links via LT-LFPS.
fsm_hints.rule: Tunnels are set up by the Connection Manager before traffic flows; transport uses credit-based flow control between adjacent routers.

anti_deadlock_rule: Credit-based (flow-controlled) transport between adjacent routers prevents head-of-line buffer overrun; isochronous tunnels (DisplayPort) are bandwidth-reserved + TMU-synchronized so they cannot be starved by best-effort PCIe/USB3 tunnels.
exit_from_reset_or_poweron: On connect: USB-C orientation + PD negotiation on CC pins, then LT-LFPS link training + lane bonding, then the Connection Manager reads router config space, builds the spanning tree, and sets up tunnels.

default_ready_state_recommendation.link_down: Lanes electrically idle; monitor SBU/CC for connect.
default_ready_state_recommendation.link_up_no_tunnel: Transport layer ready; await Connection Manager path setup.
default_ready_state_recommendation.tunnel_active: Adapters enabled; tunneled traffic flowing under flow control.

connection_manager_rule: Exactly one Connection Manager (host-resident) owns path/tunnel allocation for the fabric; routers are passive forwarders programmed by it.
tunnel_setup_rule: Each tunnel = an end-to-end path = an ordered list of per-hop {adapter, hop ID} entries programmed into every router along the route by the Connection Manager.
